Notes on the Instructions 
 
The present instructions provide important information on how to operate the plant. Compliance 
with all safety and work instructions is an essential prerequisite for safe working. 
Make sure to carefully read the instructions before starting work. 
 They are part of the product, 
must always be kept near the machine/ system and should be available for the personnel at any 
time. 
 
Also observe and comply with 
 local accident prevention regulations, 
 general safety regulations 
and 
 any internal instructions regarding work, operatio n and safety issued by the customer 
       applying to the machine's/plant’s area of operation. 
 
As the illustrations in these Operating Instructions might differ from the current plant 
configuration, they serve for information and basic understanding only. 
Deriving requirements from the illustrations in the present Operating Instructions is not possible. 
 
The enclosed operating instructions for the installed components apply alongside these operating 
instructions. Strictly observe the notes contained therein – especially the safety notes!

1. Transport, packing and storage 
1.1 Safety notes for transport 
 
Suspended Loads 
 
WARNING! 
Danger to life due to suspended loads! 
When lifting loads there is a danger to life due to falling 
or swinging parts. 
Therefore: 
– Never stand under a suspended load! 
– Note the instructions concerning the lifting poin ts 
provided. 
– Do not attach slings to projecting machine 
components or to the eyes of attached components; 
ensure that the slings are securely seated. 
– Only use approved lifting gear and slings with 
sufficient load-bearing capacity. 
– Do not use torn or frayed rope or belts. 
– Do not lay ropes and belts on sharp edges and 
corners, do not knot or twist ropes and belts. 
 
 
Off-centre Centre of Gravity 
 
WARNING! 
Danger of falling due to eccentric center of gravity! 
Packing crates can have an off-centre centre of gravity. 
If the slings are not attached correctly the packing crate 
may tip and cause fatal injuries. 
Therefore: 
– Note the markings on the packing crates. 
– Attach the crane hook in such a manner that it is  
over the centre of gravity. 
– Lift carefully and observe whether the load tips.  
If necessary, change the position of the slings.

12  
 
GB_MTP ... Einbau in M.. Reihe-01  
 
 
 
Incorrect transport 
 
CAUTION! 
Incorrect transport can cause damage! 
Incorrect transport can cause extensive damage. 
Therefore: 
– When unloading the packing units on delivery and 
during in-house transport, exercise caution and 
observe the symbols on the package. 
– Use only the attachment points provided. 
– Do not remove packaging material until the units are 
ready for assembly. 
– Machine components that are not placed on pallets :  
do not use a forklift for the delivery and the in-house 
transport of these items.

1.2 Transport 
Transporting packages  
with a crane 
 
             
 
Packages with attachment eyes can be transported with a crane 
under the following conditions: 
 The crane and lifting gear must be suitable for th e weight of the 
packages. 
 The operator must be authorised to operate the cra ne. 
Attaching: 
1. Attach ropes, belts or multi-point suspension gear  at the 
appropriate positions (see illustration). 
2. Make sure that the package is suspended evenly and , if 
necessary, note the off-centre centre of gravity. 
 
Transporting pallets with a 
crane 
 
          
 
Packages on pallets may be transported with a crane under the 
following conditions: 
 The crane and lifting gear used must be suitable f or weight of the 
packages. 
 The operator must be authorised to operate the cra ne. 
Attaching: 
1. Attach the ropes, slings or multi leg slings to th e pallet as shown 
in the illustration. 
2. Check if the packing pieces have been damaged by t he slings 
devices. Use other load-suspension devices if necessary. 
 
 
Transporting pallets with a 
forklift 
 
 
 
Packages on pallets can be transported with a forklift under the 
following conditions : 
  The forklift used must be suitable for the weight  of the 
transported units. 
  The driver must be authorised to operate the fork lift. 
Attaching : 
1.  Insert the forks of the forklift between or under  the beams of the 
pallet. 
2.  Insert the forks in until they protrude at the ot her side. 
3.  Ensure that the pallet cannot tilt when the centr e of gravity is off-
centre. 
4.  Lift the package.

1.3 Transport rack 
The magnet drums are propped up and screwed onto a transport rack for shipment. Packing 
in crates is only envisaged for shipment by sea.  
 
 
ATTENTION! 
The magnet system is positioned in 
the magnet drum with the centre of 
gravity at the bottom in order to 
reduce the danger of tipping during 
transportation. 
 
The magnet drum must not be stressed at the drum bo dy or the drum covers at the side 
during transportation. Ropes or loops are to be att ached to the two rotation supports of the 
magnet drum. 
The safety directives must be observed during trans portation. A suitable brace must be used 
for magnet drums with a diameter of up to 1,200 mm. 
The transport rack is only removed at the installation site! 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
The magnet drums can be transported by means of a f orklift if sufficient support is ensured. 
They must be protected against moisture during storage.  
For storage periods of more than a month, and at th e very latest during start-up, the two M 
12 screw plugs at the outer end of the cast rib in drum covers with a diameter of 800 mm and 
more must be opened to drain off condensation water  and any rain water that has 
penetrated. 
The dismounted magnet drum must be propped up on a device. The magnet system must be 
positioned in the magnet drum with the centre of gr avity at the bottom in order to reduce the 
danger of tipping.

1.5 Storing 
Storage of magnet drums in open space is not permit ted. They have to be protected against 
humidity, chemically aggressive atmosphere, frost a nd snow and shall therefore be stored in 
dry localities. 
 
Storing the packages Store the packages under the following conditions: 
 Do not store outdoors. 
 Store in a dry and dust-free location. 
 Do not expose to any aggressive media. 
 Protect against direct exposure to sunlight. 
 Avoid mechanical vibrations. 
 Storage temperature: +5 °C to +50 °C: 
 Relative humidity: max. 60%. 
 When storing for more than 3 months, check the ove rall condition 
of all parts and the packaging at regular intervals. If necessary, 
renew or replace the preservatives. 
NOTE! 
The packages may carry storage information in addition to the 
requirements mentioned here. Follow any such additional 
information.

2. Design and mode of operation of magnetic drum se parators  
 
The magnet drums are intended for the separation an d / or recovery of iron parts from the 
conveyed material. 
Interfering iron parts should be removed in order t o protect downstream machinery or for 
cleaning the material that has been fed. 
The material should always be fed via a conveyor gr oove or a slanting chute. The more 
evenly the material to be separated is fed into the  magnet drum, the better the iron 
separation. 
2.1 Structure 
The magnet drum consists of a non-magnetic hard manganese steel drum body with discharge 
strips and light metal cast side covers with rotation supports. These parts rotate around the 
stationary magnet system. Insofar as the iron parts in the material conveyed are magnetic, they 
are attracted by the magnet and are ejected from the rotating drum body by the discharge strips 
at the end of the magnet system. 
 
The adjustment key for adjusting the magnet system, or, in the case of smaller magnet drums, a 
bore with adjusting rods is also fixed to the shaft.

18  
 
GB_MTP ... Einbau in M.. Reihe-01  
 
2.2 “Overshot” mode of operation 
The material is fed onto the magnet drum from above . The conveyed material is transported 
over the drum at an angle of approximately 90°. Aft er a revolution of approximately 180°, the 
iron is discharged downwards at the bottom edge of the drum and ejected backwards. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Area of application 
For fine-grained material and small effects at depth, for example: 
- Coal, ore 
- Cement 
- Refuse 
- Building rubble, slag, foundry sand,  
- Wood chips 
- Cereal, fodder, nutrients   etc. 
 
 
2.3 Method of Extraction 
 
The material is fed at the side of or beneath the 
magnet drum. 
At the channel outlet, the conveyed material 
drops downwards. The iron is attracted by the 
magnet drum, discharged above it and ejected 
backwards. 
 
Area of application 
- Primarily used for preparing sheet scrap and mixe d scrap (mainly body scrap) and for 
cleaning non-ferrous scrap metal.

19  
 
GB_MTP ... Einbau in M.. Reihe-01  
 
3. Mounting - Installation 
 
Danger of crushing: 
 
 
During start-up and maintenance work, there is a risk of 
crushing by the material attracted by the magnetic field. 
 
 
 
The drum is aligned towards the conveyor groove or chute. 
The outlet ends just before the midperpendicular of the drum, 
so that material cannot slip off backwards.  
With regard to conveyor grooves, 
the outlet vibration must be taken into account and the 
distance must be selected appropriately so that the end of 
the groove does not hit the drum. 
The metal chute  
must be tilted in such a way that the conveyed material slips 
off onto the drum and does not remain on the chute. If the 
slant is very steep, ensure that the iron cannot overshoot the 
magnet drum without being braked. It may be necessary to 
suspend a mass pendulum or rubber apron in front of the 
outlet. 
 
When installing drums for extraction operation, a conveyor 
groove must be provided for the material transport.  
Consider distance between the conveying trough outlet and 
the magnetic drum casing, see data sheet "Mounting-Proposal 
for Magnetic Drum" in the appendix.

4. Adjust the magnet system 
Once the drum has been assembled, the magnet system must be placed inside the drum.  
 
Danger of injury!   ATTENTION! 
The adjustment lever must be locked in position before 
releasing the clamping screws and/or the mounting 
sets! 
- The adjustment lever turns over in an uncontrolle d 
manner when the magnet system is released. 
 
For larger drum diameters, 
the mounting sets on the outside of the bearing blocks must be loosened and the magnet 
system must be put in the working position with the help of the adjustment lever fitted.  
For smaller drum diameters, 
the clamping screws must be loosened. Using the adjusting lever, put the magnet system into 
the working position. 
Re-tighten the mounting sets and clamping screws. 
Fasten the supplied load-securing strap to the ring bolt of the adjusting lever and to the frame 
structure. This increases safety when loosening the mounting elements to adjust the system to 
prevent slipping and makes it easier to adjust the system upwards in small increments. Caution 
is advisable when loosening the load-securing strap to adjust the system downwards.

If the mounting set consisting of two pressing ring s does not slacken off once the screws

5. Use of non-magnetic material  
All structural parts that are within a circle the r adius of which corresponds to the magnet 
drum diameter (D), must be made from non-magnetic m aterial. 
The following structural parts can protrude in this area: 
a) The channel outlet of a vibrator chute or feedin g chute 
b) Connecting profiles behind the magnet drum 
c) A separating sheet below the magnet drum that sh ould be arranged so that it can be 
moved forward from the centre of the magnet drum un til it reaches the falling non-
magnetic conveyed material. 
d) Layer depth limiters in front of the magnet drum  
 Non-magnetic structural parts within the two rotat ion supports must be used within the 
area covered by the magnet drum width. 
 
All magnetisable structural parts situated within t he specified area lead to the formation of 
secondary magnets and a considerable reduction of the magnetic separation performance. 
Covering steel parts with non-magnetic sheet has no  effect. All components in the area of 
the magnetic field become magnetised and then attra ct and hold other iron components. 
This can lead to blockages and faults in the conveying route.

6. Lubricating roller bearings 
The factory-installed maintenance-free bearing unit s are lubricated with corrosion-resistant 
and non-aging roller bearing grease. 
For safety reasons, lubrication nipples are not attached. 
Owing to their design, the bearings are protected against dirt. 
 
6.1 First filling 
First at the factory is made with Retinax EP 2 by Shell AG . 
The grease has a temperature range of -30 °C to +12 0 °C 
The operating temperature of the bearings is 30 °C to 50 °C overtemperature 
 
6.2 Replacing the grease contents after carrying ou t maintenance 
To relubricate, use a lithium saponified grease of the same worked penetration. Avoid 
mixing grease types. If you have to do so, consult the manufacturer of the grease! 
Quantity of grease  approx. 30 cm³  
for a complete regrease per lubrication point. 
Maximum grease content is to be about 30-50% of the  bearing housing. Too much grease 
can lead to an increase in bearing operating temperature.

7.1 Removing the magnetic drum 
To repair the magnetic drum, it must be removed from the machine / the support frame.

2. Undo the bolted connection at the clamp bearing (2).

8. General  
 
All specifications apply for normal operating conditions. 
 
The permissible temperature range extends from   -2 0°C   to   +35°C   for electromagnetic 
drums  
and   from   -30°C   to   +100°C   for permanent magnetic drums. 
 
We reserve the right to make changes promoting the technical development. 
 
9. Disposal 
Clean the plant to be disassembled and dismantle it  according to applicable industrial safety 
and environment protection regulations. 
 Physically separate the plant from all energy supp lies and discharge stored residual energies.  
 Remove operating and auxiliary media as well as re sidual processing material and dispose of 
them in an environmentally compatible manner. 
According to the condition of the device and existing regulations, recycle dismantled parts. 
 Scrap metals. 
 Have plastic parts recycled. 
 Dispose of all other components sorted according t o material type. 
 
 
CAUTION! 
Environmental damage due to incorrect disposal! 
Electric scrap, electronic components, lead components, lubricants and other operating 
media must be treated as special waste und may be disposed of by approved disposal 
companies only! 
 
Local authorities or specialised waste management companies provide information regarding 
environmentally compatible disposal.
